title: SSC CGL 90-Day Study Plan 2026: 12-Week Plan from Basics to Mocks
description: A 12-week SSC CGL 2026 study plan from scratch at 5.5 hours a day: three phases, week-wise topic tables, mock cadence and revision loops for Tier 1.
intro: Ninety days is the most comfortable runway for a first serious attempt. It lets you rebuild school-level basics, cover every CGL topic with timed practice, and still run **two to three weeks of full mocks**. The plan assumes about 5.5 hours a day in three phases: Foundation (weeks 1 to 4), Build (weeks 5 to 8) and Test (weeks 9 to 12).

sections.title: Plan structure and daily budget
sections.body:
| Phase | Weeks | Aim |
|---|---|---|
| Foundation | 1 to 4 | Speed maths, arithmetic, DI, verbal reasoning, grammar and vocabulary habit, GA reading |
| Build | 5 to 8 | Geometry, mensuration, algebra, trigonometry, non-verbal reasoning, RC and cloze, science, topic tests |
| Test | 9 to 12 | Mocks, error analysis, revision loops, Tier 2 style practice |

**Daily budget (about 5.5 hours, six days a week):**

| Slot | Hours |
|---|---|
| Quant | 2.0 |
| Reasoning | 1.0 |
| English | 1.5 |
| General Awareness | 1.0 |

**Seventh day.** Test or revision day. Foundation and Build weeks: a sectional test and 2 hours of analysis. Test weeks: a full mock and analysis. Every night spend 15 to 20 minutes on the mistakes notebook, and revise each topic on **day 1, day 7 and day 21** after you learn it. The 12 weeks add up to 84 days; the remaining 6 days are buffer for illness, travel or catching up. Working candidates can halve the budget and stretch the same sequence to 180 days.

sections.title: Phase 1, weeks 1 to 4: foundation
sections.body:
Goal: speed and accuracy on the arithmetic backbone, plus a daily reading and vocabulary habit. Do not take full mocks yet; do one sectional test per week.

| Week | Quant (2 h) | Reasoning (1 h) | English (1.5 h) | GA (1 h) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Speed base (tables, squares, cubes, fractions), [Simplification](/quant/simplification/), [Number System](/quant/number-system/) | [Series](/reasoning/series/), [Analogy](/reasoning/analogy/) | [Grammar essentials](/english/grammar-essentials/): parts of speech, tenses, agreement; 8 new words a day | Current affairs habit begins ([current affairs](/current-affairs/)), [Ancient history](/ga/ancient-history/) |
| 2 | [Percentage](/quant/percentage/), [Ratio and Proportion](/quant/ratio-proportion/), [Average](/quant/average/) | [Classification](/reasoning/classification/), [Coding-Decoding](/reasoning/coding-decoding/) | Grammar: articles, prepositions, modals; [Spelling](/english/spelling/) | [Medieval](/ga/medieval-history/) and [Modern history](/ga/modern-history/) |
| 3 | [Profit, Loss and Discount](/quant/profit-loss-discount/), [Interest](/quant/interest/), [Mixture and alligation](/quant/mixture-alligation/) | [Missing number](/reasoning/missing-number/), [Mathematical operations](/reasoning/mathematical-operations/), [Dictionary order](/reasoning/dictionary-order/) | [Error spotting](/english/error-spotting/), [Sentence improvement](/english/sentence-improvement/) | [Polity](/ga/polity/) |
| 4 | [Time and Work](/quant/time-work/), [Time, Speed and Distance](/quant/time-speed-distance/), [HCF and LCM](/quant/hcf-lcm/) | [Syllogism](/reasoning/syllogism/), [Order and ranking](/reasoning/order-ranking/) | [Synonyms and antonyms](/english/synonyms-antonyms/), [Idioms](/english/idioms-phrases/), [One-word substitution](/english/one-word-substitution/) | [Economy](/ga/economy/) |

Weekly test day: one sectional test on that week's subjects, then analysis. In place of the sectional test at the end of week 4, take your first **diagnostic full mock** just to measure where you stand; do not worry about the score.

sections.title: Phase 2, weeks 5 to 8: build
sections.body:
Goal: finish the syllabus, with the largest Quant blocks getting the most time. See the [weightage](/exams/ssc-cgl/weightage/) page for the per-topic counts. Add a **topic test** (10 to 15 questions, timed) after every topic.

| Week | Quant (2 h) | Reasoning (1 h) | English (1.5 h) | GA (1 h) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | [Data Interpretation](/quant/data-interpretation/) (all types), [Statistics](/quant/statistics/) | [Seating arrangement](/reasoning/seating-arrangement/), [Blood relations](/reasoning/blood-relations/), [Direction and distance](/reasoning/direction-distance/) | [Reading comprehension](/english/reading-comprehension/): one passage a day | [Indian geography](/ga/indian-geography/) |
| 6 | [Geometry](/quant/geometry/): lines, triangles, circles, quadrilaterals | [Venn diagrams](/reasoning/venn-diagrams/), [Statement-conclusion](/reasoning/statement-conclusion/), [Cube and dice](/reasoning/cube-dice/) | [Cloze test](/english/cloze-test/): one passage a day | [Biology](/ga/biology/) |
| 7 | [Mensuration 2D](/quant/mensuration-2d/) and [3D](/quant/mensuration-3d/), [Algebra](/quant/algebra/) | [Counting figures](/reasoning/counting-figures/), [Mirror and water image](/reasoning/mirror-water-image/), [Paper folding](/reasoning/paper-folding-cutting/) | [Sentence rearrangement](/english/sentence-rearrangement/), [Fill in the blanks](/english/fill-in-the-blanks/), [Active-passive](/english/active-passive/), [Direct-indirect](/english/direct-indirect/) | [Physics](/ga/physics/), [Chemistry](/ga/chemistry/) |
| 8 | [Trigonometry](/quant/trigonometry/), [Heights and distances](/quant/heights-distances/), Geometry revisit | [Embedded figures](/reasoning/embedded-figures/), [Figure series](/reasoning/figure-series/), weak types | Vocabulary revision (list of 150 words), RC and cloze timed | [Static GK](/ga/static-gk/), [Art and culture](/ga/art-culture/), [World geography](/ga/world-geography/) |

Test days in this phase: week 5 sectional (Quant), week 6 sectional (Quant + Reasoning), week 7 sectional (English + GA), week 8 **full mock**. From week 7, add 15 minutes a day of keyboard practice on the [typing test](/exams/ssc-cgl/typing-test/); the data-entry speed test is qualifying in Tier 2.

sections.title: Phase 3, weeks 9 to 12: test and refine
sections.body:
Goal: convert knowledge into speed. Each mock is followed by at least 2 hours of analysis. Use the [mocks](/exams/ssc-cgl/mocks/) page for full-length practice.

| Week | Mocks | Other work (5.5 h days) |
|---|---|---|
| 9 | 2 full mocks | Day-wise repair of weak topics from the diagnostic and week-8 mocks; re-solve all wrong questions |
| 10 | 3 full mocks (alternate days) | One section drill per day: 25 questions in 15 minutes; revise formulas and idioms |
| 11 | 3 full mocks | Tier 2 style practice: harder Maths sets, a longer English set (45 questions), 25 GA questions; revision of weak chapters |
| 12 | 3 full mocks | Last two days only: formula sheet, mistakes notebook, vocabulary; rest the day before the exam |

On mock days, attempt at your expected shift time. In the last week stop learning new topics; use only the formula sheet, the mistakes notebook, and the idiom and vocabulary lists. Use the [score calculator](/exams/ssc-cgl/score-calculator/) to check your normalised-style estimate, and compare your trend (not one score) with the [cutoffs](/exams/ssc-cgl/cutoffs/) page.

sections.title: Revision system that runs across all 12 weeks
sections.body:
| Loop | What you revise | When |
|---|---|---|
| Daily | New words (8), 20 current-affairs points, last day's mistakes | 30 minutes, any slot |
| Weekly | The week's topics via a timed 25-question set | Test day |
| Fortnightly | Formula sheet end to end, idioms and one-word list | One 90-minute block |
| Phase end | Whole mistakes notebook, grouped by topic | Last 2 days of weeks 4, 8 and 12 |

The 1-7-21 rule: revisit each topic one day, one week and three weeks after learning it. That is why Phase 1 topics get touched again in weeks 5, 6 and 8.

sections.title: Linking the plan to Tier 2
sections.body: Tier 1 does not decide the final merit; Tier 2 Paper 1 (out of 390) does. Use weeks 5 to 8 of this plan at full depth, because Tier 2 Maths and English draw on the same chapters with harder questions. After Tier 1, you can run weeks 5 to 12 again with Tier 2 mocks; see the Tier 2 strategy guide for the pattern, marks and sectional approach. Check the [exam pattern](/exams/ssc-cgl/exam-pattern/) and [syllabus](/exams/ssc-cgl/syllabus/) pages for the current structure.

faqs.q: Is 90 days enough for SSC CGL from scratch?
faqs.a: For a graduate with school-level maths, yes, if you can give 5 to 6 hours daily and take mocks seriously. Many selections come from 3 to 5 months of focused preparation. Nothing is guaranteed, but 90 days leaves enough time for one full syllabus pass and about 8 to 10 mocks.

faqs.q: How many mocks should I take in 90 days?
faqs.a: Roughly 12 to 14 full mocks (one diagnostic mock in week 4, one in week 8, then 3 a week in weeks 9 to 12), plus weekly sectional tests. Analysis time per mock should be at least twice the attempt time.

faqs.q: What if I can study only 3 hours a day?
faqs.a: Run the same sequence at half the daily budget over about 150 to 180 days, keeping the weekly test day intact. Do not cut mocks to fit the schedule.

faqs.q: Should I start with Quant or English?
faqs.a: Start both in week 1. Quant needs speed built over weeks, and English needs a daily reading and vocabulary habit. GA reading fits into small daily slots.

faqs.q: When do I start Tier 2 preparation?
faqs.a: Weeks 5 to 8 already prepare the ground. Tier 2 specific work (harder Maths, 45 English questions, the Computer module and the data-entry speed test) starts after Tier 1 or from week 11 of this plan.
